question: Can the harness replace torch as the CUDA-context gate, so a 20 GB PyTorch image is not needed to evaluate one boolean?
answer: Yes. Run beside the torch gate on the same device, --mode cuda-probe created a context and read the device memory; both gates passed and agreed. torch is no longer load-bearing on the prove path.

device_memory_cross_check.note: 47,699,722,240 B is 45,488 MiB of addressable device memory against nvidia-smi's 46,068 MiB board total; the difference is reserved, not missing

what_this_unblocks: the gate was the only reason the drivers needed a PyTorch image. A slim CUDA runtime image can now gate properly.
what_still_blocks_a_slim_image: sshd. Direct SSH needs openssh-server in the image; RunPod's own images carry it and a stock nvidia/cuda image does not, so push-and-launch.sh cannot deliver scripts or start tmux and the PTY-only proxy is the trap that cost wazabi's r114 a pod. A slim image therefore needs openssh-server baked in (hence a registry) or the entrypoint-driven design, which exists and has never run.
limits: one device, one card; the probe has not been run against a host that fails it, so its negative path is untested
the A5000 refused twice, so this ran on an A40; the gate is card-independent

correction.note: Overstated. sshd is still required, but not from the image: Runpod's documented container start command installs openssh-server at boot, create-pod takes entrypoint/cmd, and startSsh:true injects the account keys as $PUBLIC_KEY. So a slim image needs neither a registry nor the entrypoint design -- one apt (~10-20 s) against ~110 s of image pull. nvidia/cuda:12.8.1-base-ubuntu24.04 is 101 MB compressed against the PyTorch image's 10,564 MB and installs cuda-cudart-12-8, the only CUDA library the binary links dynamically. Start command: scripts/gpu/slim-pod-start-command.sh. Unmeasured.
